correctness.rationale: For every singular 3-cube, its six boundary squares admit cellular fillings by an oriented rigid quadrilateral or a 1-dimensional backtrack-null disk. They assemble to a sphere in X. Because pi2(X)=0 its signed cellular 2-chain represents zero, and because X has no cellular 3-chains that chain vanishes coefficientwise; an initially supported square must have another supported face. Thus 2-monophobic. Triangle-free implies 1-quasimonophobic, so Jamil–Behrens Theorem 7 yields integral H2 comparison. For C_m Cartesian C_n (m,n>=5), the square completion is the aspherical torus and its square-boundary kernel is Z. Finite exhaustive checks independently confirm all 245 anchored 3cube maps for five toroidal sizes and show failures for length-four factors.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies a structural topological sufficient condition for monophobicity, replacing intractable enumeration of normalized singular cubes by an asphericity check. It yields an all-parameter nonzero integral H2 computation for canonical toroidal graph families, a natural first two-dimensional example beyond the published Greene spheres. Non-triviality is the structural asphericity bridge; finite exact checks are corroborative, not the value claim.
